How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow
all speakers to address the City Council.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the online public
comment form at Public Comment. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00
P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for
their consideration, but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after
4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – MARCH 2025

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2024-2025 Adopted Investment

  D. APPOINTMENTS TO INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGENCIES [RESOLUTION NO.
  25-15]

  The Mayor is responsible for appointing members of the City Council to serve
  on various local and regional committees, as well as liaisons for City initiatives.
  In addition, it is necessary for the Council to take formal action to designate the
  new Mayor to serve as the Delegate to the Los Angeles County Sanitation

  Recommended Action:

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – April 15, 2025  3
   Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 25-15 confirming
  the Mayor’s appointments of Council Members to serve as delegates, alternates
  and liaisons to various agencies and committees.

  E. THEATRE FEE REDUCTION REQUEST BY SAN GABRIEL MISSION HIGH
  SCHOOL

  San Gabriel Mission High School has requested a waiver of theatre rental fees
  for their upcoming graduation ceremony, scheduled for Thursday, May 29,
  2025. The request is for a $5,851.30 fee reduction, to reduce their total rental
  cost to $5,000. The City has budgeted $10,000 in its annual Rental Subsidy
  account, account number 152-3532, from which this waiver would be charged.
  Approval of fee waivers decreases the Revenue that is received by the Mission
  Playhouse. Should the City Council approve staff’s recommendation of waiving
  $2,475, which covers the costs associated with the theatre and ancillary space
  rental, Mission Playhouse revenue for account number 152-3532 will be
  reduced accordingly.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve staff’s recommendation to
  grant a partial waiver of the San Gabriel Mission Playhouse rental fee in the
  amount of $2,475 for the San Gabriel Mission High School’s graduation
  ceremony on May 29, 2025.

  F. APPROVAL OF A TRIP TO TAIWAN FOR MAYOR MENCHACA AND
  COUNCILMEMBER WU TO TRAVEL TO NEW TAIPEI CITY TO VISIT THE 2025
  WORLD MASTERS GAMES AT NO COST TO THE CITY

  Several weeks ago, Mayor Hou Yu-ih of New Taipei City, Taiwan (R.O.C.) invited
  then-Mayor Wu and Vice Mayor Menchaca to travel to Taiwan to visit the 2025
  World Masters Games. The trip will be paid for directly by New Taipei City and
  will not have a financial impact on the City of San Gabriel. Government Code
  Section 18950.1 allows for travel costs to be paid for by a foreign government
  entity provided that the City makes a finding that the travel is for governmental
  purposes and designates the agency members who will be travelling.
  Government Code Section 89506 exempts those payments from the gift
  limitations applicable to public officials. New Taipei City will be covering airfare,

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – April 15, 2025  4
   travel, hotel, and food costs. Any incidental expenses will be paid directly by
  the Councilmembers from their personal funds.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council find that the proposed trip to Taiwan
  for the 2025 World Masters Games is for governmental purposes and authorize
  Mayor Menchaca and Councilmember Wu to travel on behalf of the City.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ORDINANCE NO. 716 AMENDING CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO HEDGE HEIGHTS IN THE RESIDENTIAL
  ZONES (ZTA24-004) – INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING

  The proposed zone text amendment would remove height limitations for
  hedges in residential zones. Hedges in residential zones would continue to be
  regulated by existing maintenance and safety standards. Should a hedge in a
  residential zone cause a hazard to the public by obscuring visibility at any public
  right-of-way, road intersection or pedestrian, it shall be the responsibility of the
  property owner to trim, relocate, or remove the hedge so as to remedy such a
  condition. Additionally, if any hedge in the parkway planting areas planted
  immediately adjacent to a respective real property is determined by the City to
  be hazardous, then it shall be the responsibility of the property owner to trim,
  relocate, or remove the hedge so as to remedy such a condition. The Fiscal Year
  2024-2025 Adopted Budget includes the cost for required legal publication
  (Account No. 121-702-00-65-000) and codification (Account No. 121-702-00-
  22-000) of the ordinance, if adopted by the City Council.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed
  amendments were reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA). This project is exempted from the requirements of CEQA, per
  Guidelines Section 15303, Class 3 (New Construction or Conversion of Small
  Structures). Accessory structures including garages, carports, patios, swimming
  pools, and fences.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – April 15, 2025  5
   1. Conduct the public hearing and discuss proposed Ordinance No. 716;

  2. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 716 by title only:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF SAN
  GABRIEL, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING CHAPTER 153 (ZONING CODE)
  OF THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO HEDGE
  HEIGHTS IN THE RESIDENTIAL ZONES.

  3. Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second reading
  and adoption of the Ordinance for the next Regular City Council
  meeting. The Ordinance would then become effective 30 days after
  adoption.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. AGREEMENT WITH GRIZZLY ENTERTAINMENT FOR AN ENHANCED
  DRONE SHOW FOR THE 2025 INDEPENDENCE DAY CELEBRATION IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $71,000 [RESOLUTION NO. 25-17]

  On December 19, 2023, the City Council approved an agreement with Grizzly
  Entertainment for the City’s first drone show. The Independence Day event was
  held on July 3, 2024, at Gabrielino High School. To further build on that event,
  staff proposes to work once again with Grizzly Entertainment to provide an
  enhanced show that has a longer run time. The total cost for the agreement
  with Grizzly Entertainment for the quoted July 3 enhanced drone show is
  $71,000. For the 2024 event, the cost for the drone show was $45,000. Staff
  anticipates that other event costs will be close to the costs last year and the
  majority of costs will be included in the Fiscal Year 2025-2026 budget. The Fiscal
  Year 2024-2025 budget for this Independence Day event is $50,250. With this,
  staff recommends that the City Council appropriate funding from the City’s
  General Fund to cover the cost for the enhanced drone show in the amount of
  $26,000 to Non-Departmental Special Events account number 121-714-00-27-
  047. Any sponsorship costs brought in will help to offset these additional costs.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines, as it has no potential to
  result in any change to the environment.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – April 15, 2025  6
   Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve a show with Grizzly Entertainment on Thursday, July 3, 2025, to
  include lights, lasers, up to 500 drones, at a cost of $71,000 at Gabrielino
  High School.

  2. Authorize the City Manager to sign the agreement with Grizzly
  Entertainment.

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute a Memorandum of
  Understanding (MOU) and any other necessary documents with San
  Gabriel Unified School District pending review and approval by the City
  Attorney.

  4. Designate two City Councilmembers to serve on the Council Committee
  for the Independence Day Celebration.

  5. Adopt Resolution No. 25-17 appropriating $26,000 from the City’s
  General Fund into account #121-714-00-27-047 for the Independence
  Day event.

MINUTES OF APRIL 15, 2025
  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Menchaca called the special meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at
  6:03 P.M. on Tuesday, April 15, 2025, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South
  Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Ding.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Tony Ding, Jorge Herrera Avila, John Wu, Vice Mayor
  Eric Chan, and Mayor Denise Menchaca.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Community Services Director

I
  Rebecca Perez, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Fire Chief
  Steven Wallace; Human Resources/Risk Management
  Director Edward Macias, Finance Director William
  Kaholokula, Police Chief Edward Elizalde, Acting Public
  Works Director/City Engineer Szeka Cheng, Acting
  Community Development Director Samantha Tewasart,
  and Assistant City Clerk Marilyn Bonus.

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT - Special Meeting of April 1. 2025

  A. CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR (GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6)

  City Negotiators - City Manager Lazzaretto, City Attorney Lemieux, and Human
  Resources/Risk Management Director Macias

  Regarding the following Employee Organizations - San Gabriel Police Officer's
  Association, San Gabriel Police Management Group, San Gabriel Firefighter's
  Association, San Gabriel Fire Management Group and all Unrepresented
  Employees.

I  There was no reportable action.

  B. CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL- EXISTING LITIGATION (GOVERNMENT
  CODE §54956.9)

  Tappan Zee v. City of San Gabriel et al., COCA Case No: 2:21-CV-06167.

  There was no reportable action.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 7  April 15, 2025
   Chief City Clerk Clark provided information for the public on how to view the meeting.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Mayor Menchaca approved the agenda order.

  2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. RECOGNITION OF INCOMING MAYOR AND VICE MAYOR AND OUTGOING

I  MAYOR

  Congresswoman Judy Chu administered a ceremonial oath of office to Mayor
  Menchaca.

  Former Arcadia Mayor Peter Amundson administered a ceremonial oath of office
  to Vice Mayor Chan.

  The following recognized incoming Mayor Menchaca and Vice Mayor Chan, and
  outgoing Mayor Wu:

  •  Congresswoman Judy Chu
  •  Amber Giang, District Representative for California Senator Sasha Renee
  Perez
  •  Jayson Hugh, Field Representative for Assemblymember Mike Fong
  •  Pablo Morales, Field Deputy for Los Angeles County Supervisor Hilda Solis
  •  Alhambra Mayor Katherine Lee and Council Member Adele Andrade-Stadler
  •  Monterey Park Mayor Vinh Ngo, Mayor Pro Tern Elizabeth Yang, and Council
  Member Henry Lo

I  •
  •
  •
  Rosemead Mayor Margaret Clark
  City of El Monte (certificates)
  City of La Puente (certificates)
  •  Mike Eng, Board Member, California Unemployment Insurance Appeals
  Board
  •  Geoff Kahan (for Vice Mayor Chan)
  •  Victor Gau and Frank Yeh, IAPAC, AAAA, AATF, and San Gabriel Hope Lions
  Club
  •  Helena Sun of C.W.B.A.C.
  •  Denise Gotch
  •  Cerritos Councilmember Jennifer Hong

  Mayor Menchaca presented outgoing Mayor Wu with a gavel plaque on behalf of
  the City and Council.

  Outgoing Mayor Wu commented on his year of service and goals achieved;
  thanked his Council colleagues, City Manager Lazzaretto, City staff, and his mentor,
  former Mayor John Harrington; and expressed his confidence in Mayor Menchaca

I  and best wishes to incoming Vice Mayor Chan.

  Vice Mayor Chan thanked outgoing Mayor Wu and congratulated incoming Mayor
  Menchaca, thanked his Council colleagues for selecting him as Vice Mayor, thanked
  his family and friends for their support, and stated he is looking forward to serving
  all residents of San Gabriel.

  Mayor Menchaca expressed gratitude to those attending meeting and those with
  her in spirit, thanked her husband and children for their support, thanked City staff
  for working alongside Council and her Council colleagues for their partnership,

  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 7  April 15, 2025
   reflected on her first term as Mayor, and commented on her goals for the coming
  year.

  Council Member Herrera Avila thanked community members and elected officials
  who attended the meeting for their support, commended outgoing Mayor Wu for
  his successful term as Mayor, commended Mayor Menchaca for her first term and
  stated he is looking forward to her second term, and congratulated incoming Vice
  Mayor Chan.

I  Council Member Ding commended outgoing Mayor Wu, and congratulated
  incoming Mayor Menchaca and Vice Mayor Chan.

  B. CITY'S BIRTHDAY

  Mayor Menchaca made the presentation.

  C. OUTSTANDING OLDER AMERICAN RIAZ (RICK) KHAN

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Allen Co commented on his family's challenges related to housing in San Gabriel.

  Mary Garcia, resident, expressed concern about on-going maintenance issues at the

  4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Council Member Herrera Avila requested that item 4F be pulled for separate

I  discussion.

  approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4C and 4E as presented, and Item 4D as
  amended.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, HERRERA AVILA, WU, CHAN, MENCHACA
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 7  April 15, 2025
   ABSENT:  NONE

  Regarding Item 4F, Council Member Herrera Avila questioned whether Mayor
  Menchaca and Council Member Wu should recuse themselves from this item. Assistant
  City Attorney Koczanowicz stated there was no legal conflict and they could
  participate. Council Member Herrera Avila requested their voluntary recusal and a
  postponement on consideration of the item until a formal travel policy could be
  adopted, and expressed various concerns related to the proposed trip.

I  A motion was made by Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Council Member Ding, to
  approve Item 4F.

  Discussion included that Council has already set policy that each proposed trip will be
  considered on a case-by-case basis; benefits to the City of the proposed trip; contents
  of the staff report; benefit of a formal policy for the future; the proposed trip's
  compliance with Fair Political Practices Commission (FPPC) regulations; availability on
  video and in minutes of previous Council discussion on the subject; importance of
  connecting City staff with Sister Cities; and Form 700 disclosures related to the trip.

  Motion carried by a vote of 4-1 as follows:

  AYES:  DING, WU, CHAN, MENCHACA
  NOES:  HERRERA AVILA
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

I  The City Council approved:

  1.  Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of March 18, 2025.

  3.  Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of April 1, 2025.
  4.  Minutes of the Special City Council Meeting of April 8, 2025.

  The City Council approved March 20 and 28, 2025, Material Demands for the

  The City Council received and filed the Cash and Investment Report for March 2025.

  D. APPOINTMENTS TO INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGENCIES [RESOLUTION NO.

I  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 25-15 confirming the Mayor's
  appointments of Council Members to serve as delegates, alternates and liaisons to

  E. THEATRE FEE REDUCTION REQUEST BY SAN GABRIEL MISSION HIGH
  SCHOOL

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  District pending review and approval by the City Attorney.

  4. Designate two City Council members to serve on the Council Committee for the

  5. Adopt Resolution No. 25-17 appropriating $26,000 from the City's General
